questions.text: A tower crane uniformly lifts a steel beam 5 m long with a cross-section of 0.01 m² to a height of 15 m in a horizontal position. Find the work done by the crane. The density of the beam material is 7800 kg/m³. g = 10 m/s².
How much work does a person do when lifting a body of mass 2 kg with an acceleration of 3 m/s² to a height of 1 m? g = 10 m/s².
A load begins to be lifted vertically upward with constant acceleration. How many times smaller is the work done in the first second of motion than the work done in the next, second second?
A load of mass 1 kg is lifted vertically upward on a string with constant acceleration. In 2 s the tension force of the rope does 48 J of work. Find the acceleration of the load. g = 10 m/s².

How much work does a force of 20 N do when lifting a load of mass 2 kg with an acceleration of 5 m/s² along an inclined plane to a height of 2.5 m? The force acts parallel to the inclined plane. Neglect friction. g = 10 m/s².

A body of mass 20 kg is lifted along an inclined plane to a height of 6 m, traveling 10 m along the plane. If the pulling force is parallel to the plane and the coefficient of friction is 0.2, find the work done by the friction force (magnitude). g = 10 m/s².

A body of mass 0.5 kg slides from the top of an inclined plane of height 7 m down to its base. The angle of inclination of the plane to the horizontal is 45° and the coefficient of friction is 0.2. Find the work done by the friction force (magnitude). g = 10 m/s².
A body is thrown horizontally from some height at 10 m/s. After how many seconds will the kinetic energy of the body double? g = 10 m/s².
A stone is thrown horizontally from some height at 20 m/s. 4 s after the throw, the kinetic energy of the stone is 3000 J. What is the mass of the stone? g = 10 m/s².
A body of mass 3 kg is thrown from the ground at an angle of 60° to the horizontal at a speed of 8 m/s. Find the kinetic energy of the body at the highest point of its rise.
At what angle to the horizontal must a stone be thrown so that its kinetic energy at the point of maximum height is 25% of its kinetic energy at the point of launch? Give the answer in degrees.
A car starts uniformly accelerated motion. How many times smaller is the change in its kinetic energy during the first 10 s of motion than the change during the next 10 s?
A basketball of mass 0.8 kg flies at 10 m/s. A player catches the ball and stops it in 0.1 s. What average power does the player develop? (Give the absolute value of the power.)
The speed of a freely falling body of mass 4 kg increased from 2 m/s to 8 m/s over some distance. Find the work done by gravity over this distance.

A stone of mass 200 g was thrown from a horizontal surface at an angle to the horizontal and landed on the same surface at a distance of 40 m after 4 s. How much work was spent on the throw? g = 10 m/s².
A bullet of mass 5 g flying horizontally at 800 m/s pierces a board and emerges from it at 400 m/s. Find the absolute value of the work done on the bullet by the resistive force of the board.
A bullet flying at some speed hits a bag of sand and penetrates it to a depth of 15 cm. If a bullet of the same mass moves at twice the speed, to what depth (in cm) will it penetrate the sand?

A stone is thrown horizontally from a tower 30 m high. Find the potential energy of the stone 2 s after the start of motion. The mass of the stone is 0.2 kg. The potential energy at the ground surface is zero. g = 10 m/s².
A body of mass 2 kg is thrown from the ground at 6 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. By how much does its potential energy increase when the body reaches the highest point of its rise?

Three uniform rectangular slabs, each of mass 80 kg and thickness 0.2 m, lie horizontally on the ground next to each other. What minimum work must be done to stack the slabs one on top of another? g = 10 m/s².
A thin crowbar 1.5 m long with a mass of 10 kg lies on a horizontal surface. What minimum work must be done to stand it vertically on the ground? g = 10 m/s².

By how much does the potential energy of a block of mass 200 kg change when it is moved from a horizontal position to a vertical position? The block is 1 m long and has a square cross-section with a side of 20 cm. g = 10 m/s².

A thin chain 2 m long with a mass of 5 kg lies on a horizontal plane. What is the minimum work done in lifting the chain by one end until its lower end is at a height above the plane equal to the length of the chain? g = 10 m/s².
What minimum work (in kJ) must be done to pump out to the ground surface the water filling half of a pool with an area of 10 m² and a depth of 2 m? g = 10 m/s².

A deep pool with an area of 15 m² is filled with water to a depth of 1 m and is divided exactly in the middle by a vertical partition. The partition is slowly moved so that it divides the pool in the ratio 1:3. What work (in kJ) is done in the process?
A compressed spring with a stiffness of 10 kN/m has a reserve of potential energy of 50 J. By how many centimeters is the spring compressed?
If a spring is compressed by 1 cm under a force of 30 N, find the work (J) that must be done to compress it by 20 cm.
